rites.name: Dronarnath
rites.text: Dronarnath is the concept of a low, resonant hum that ran through Khogar during the Singing, when the first roots of the world condensed out of sound. It is remembered as the force that taught matter where to hold its shape.

rites.name: Mielys
rites.text: Mielys is the concept of song-as-law in Khogar, the rhythm by which the first roots of the world were pressed into shape during the Singing. In the Holy Age its devotees keep the tempo of flame and temple, and their vows are said to hold because the chant holds them.

rites.name: Vhouktok
rites.text: Vhouktok is a concept of the Khogar Martial Realm, a force of judgment that the Courts of the second Era set against rival powers during the trials that preceded the building of the doors between worlds. Its strength lies in how it bends the terms of a contest rather than in raw destruction, though it can also break a stone ward when provoked.

rites.name: Kogak
rites.text: Kogak is a concept of the Khogar Courts, the principle of a trial that tests a claimant before a council of judges. It was invoked during the Age of Sundering to decide which realms kept their doors when landfall broke the old bonds between worlds.

rites.name: Tensamvarum
rites.text: Tensamvarum is the concept of tension held in a bowed branch, the stored strength that a grove's roots and trunks keep ready for storms. In the Seeding of Khogar it was bound into the Weave as the quiet pressure beneath the first sovereign's growing kingdoms.
